methodology.target: Restore each non-defense occupation, pay plan and grade to its December 31, 2024 level (last OPM snapshot before January 19, 2025).
methodology.positions: Sum of positive baseline-minus-comparison headcount differences within occupation/pay-plan/grade groups across non-defense agencies. Growth in another group does not offset a decline. Promotions, reclassifications and ordinary turnover can contribute; these are not identified individual job losses.
methodology.cost: For each occupation/pay-plan/grade group, net positions to restore x baseline mean reported annualized adjusted basic pay for that group; loaded x1.33 for benefits and overhead. This is a restoration scenario at baseline pay, not an exact current hiring cost. Base payroll excludes the loading.
methodology.salary_imputation: Baseline mean reported salary in the same occupation/pay-plan/grade group prices each net decline. Groups with no reported salary fall back to the same pay-plan/grade, then occupation, then the non-defense mean. Withheld salaries within a group are represented by its reported mean; values outside [10k, 500k] are unreported.
methodology.defense: Defense civilians are excluded from the headline; September defense submissions are incomplete (~10,000 records missing).
methodology.caveats: Net headcount change is not a count of layoffs. Some turnover is ordinary attrition. Restoring to the pre-transition level is a policy choice, not an established staffing requirement.
